attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post, not a quotation of someone else.

semantics.note: The drafter correctly reads 'that' as turning input into a logical form and reasoning over it. The two parts (classical AI had only limited success; Gemini still struggles) are both kept, in the present and past tense used.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary: 'limited success' means real but bounded achievements without broad reliable coverage, and Gemini is judged on reporting before the post. It is not stretched for or against the speaker.

evidence.note: A 2019 scholarly survey says early rule-based semantic parsers were domain-specific and brittle, which fits limited general success.
Independent December 2023 tests found Gemini Pro failing at tracking objects and doing worse on longer reasoning questions. This was published before the post.
Winograd's 1971 SHRDLU worked only in a toy world. That is bounded success, which is consistent with 'limited' and does not contradict it.
Google's own disclosure of Gemini's progress, including a 62.4% MMMU score. It shows advances, not broad reliability, so it does not contradict the claim.

reviews.rationale: Historical research shows classical systems were domain-bound and brittle, and independent tests from before the post show Gemini Pro failing at reasoning. The counterevidence shows only bounded achievements, not broadly reliable interpretation and reasoning, so the contradiction condition is not met.

semantics.note: 'Certainly won't come close to eliminating' is firm, so it is a scorable forecast. The hedged 'may reduce' part is rightly not treated as a separate prediction. No deadline was given.

contract.note: Reading 'eliminating' as near-zero hallucination across representative factual tasks is fair. The speaker gave no threshold or task scope, so how those are read shapes any outcome.

evidence.note: The 2024 CRAG benchmark found 17–25% hallucination in leading RAG systems. That shows failures at the time, but not the open-ended future outcome.
Vectara's February 2025 leaderboard shows about 0.7% on document summarisation. That is a narrow task that does not isolate retrieval's effect, so it does not meet the early-contradiction rule.
Vectara's November 2025 harder benchmark found best rates around 3.3% and many above 10%. It is summarisation only.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with no deadline. No dated, reproducible demonstration shows broad near-zero hallucination attributable to RAG, so the early-resolution rule is not met. Continued failures cannot confirm an open-ended negative prediction, so the forecast remains unresolved.
